title: Divided Powers, Integral Forms, and Quantum Highest Weights

items.title: Kashiwara's skew derivations $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ on the negative half
items.statement:
Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with its generated
subalgebras $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ and root gradings
$U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ of
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]
($Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$, height $\operatorname{ht}$ of
[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]). Fix $i\in I$ and
write $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, so that $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j$ and
$q_i-q_i^{-1}\ne0$.

For every $P\in U_q^-$ there exist unique elements $Q,R\in U_q^-$ with

$$E_iP-PE_i=\frac{K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}.$$

Define the **Kashiwara skew derivations** $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ by

$$e_i'(P):=R\qquad\text{and}\qquad e_i''(P):=Q .$$

Thus $e_i'$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i^{-1}$ and
$e_i''$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i$ in the
commutator with $E_i$. The maps have the following properties, all proved in
the Verification below.

(a) $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, vanish on $1$, and
$e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ for all $j\in I$.

(b) (Twisted Leibniz rules) For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$, with the actual
weight $\operatorname{wt}(x)\in Q$ of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
$$e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i'(y),\qquad e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i''(y).$$

(c) (Commutation with the generators) For all $j\in I$ and all $y\in U_q^-$,
$$e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y,\qquad e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y,$$

equivalently $e_i'F_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'+\delta_{ij}$ and
$e_i''F_j=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''+\delta_{ij}$ as operators on $U_q^-$.

(d) (Grading, height and nilpotence) For every $\nu\in Q_+$,

$$e_i'\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr),\ e_i''\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr)\ \subseteq\ U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)],$$

the right-hand side being $0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. In particular both
maps raise the actual weight by $\alpha_i$, lower the positive height by one,
and are locally nilpotent: $(e_i')^{k}(P)=(e_i'')^{k}(P)=0$ for $k$ larger than
the height of the degree of a homogeneous $P$.

(e) (Bar compatibility) Let $\psi$ be the semilinear algebra involution
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
Then $e_i''=\psi\,e_i'\,\psi$ on $U_q^-$.

The commutator construction also fixes the orientation: the
$K_i^{-1}$-coefficient is $e_i'$ and the $K_i$-coefficient is $e_i''$. The
twists $q_i^{\pm\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}$ in (b) are the twists
of the corresponding coefficient maps of the negative-half coproduct in the
source's dictionary; the explicit commutator computation used here is the
definition of record, and no imaginary-simple-root convention is needed, since
every Cartan datum of this library has $a_{ii}=2$.

references.title: Kyeonghoon Jeong, Seok-Jin Kang and Masaki Kashiwara, Crystal Bases for Quantum Generalized Kac-Moody Algebras, arXiv:math/0305390

items.title: The Lusztig divided-power integral form $U_A$
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.
items.strategy: A definition with its integrality conventions fixed. $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ is a subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$, and it is not a principal ideal domain (for example (2,q-1) is not principal). No torsion-free-to-free inference over this ring is permitted. Every $T_{i,c,t}$ is a finite product of elements of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$: each numerator is a difference of two toral monomials and each denominator $q_i^{s}-q_i^{-s}$ is a nonzero element of the field $\mathbb Q(q)$ because $q$ is transcendental and $d_i>0$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]). Hence each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$, so the toral elements commute with each other and with all $K_h$; this commutativity is used in the reordering lemma. The generators are homogeneous: $E_i^{(r)}$ has root degree $r\alpha_i$, $F_i^{(r)}$ has degree $-r\alpha_i$, and $K_h,T_{i,c,t}$ have degree $0$; therefore $U_A$ is generated by homogeneous elements and is graded by $Q$, and its intersection with $U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule. Since $E_i,F_i,K_h$ generate $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ as a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra, the $\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. No choice principle is used, and no claim is made here about which products of these generators are independent: the division into the three subalgebras is the subject of the triangular-decomposition theorem.

items.title: Quantum weight modules, weights in $P$, and integrability
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group
with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), with root lattice $Q$,
simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ and integer pairing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$, and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with generators $E_i,F_i,K_h$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The lattice $P$ plays
the role of the integral weights of the classical theory
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]); the pairing need not
be perfect, and no identification $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$ is
assumed anywhere.

A **$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module** is a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $M$
together with a direct sum decomposition

$$M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$$

(an internal direct sum of $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspaces, only finitely many nonzero
on each vector) such that, for all $\mu\in P$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$,

$$K_h\ \text{acts on}\ M_\mu\ \text{by the scalar}\ q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle},\qquad E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i},\qquad F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}.$$

The subspaces $M_\mu$ are the **chosen label-weight spaces**: the grading is
part of the structure and is not reconstructed from the action, because the
pairing may have a kernel. **Morphisms** of $P$-graded type-one weight modules
are the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module maps $f\colon M\to N$ with
$f(M_\mu)\subseteq N_\mu$ for every $\mu$; the weight submodules and quotients
considered on this page are those with the induced grading (Verification, step 2.2).

The module is **integrable** if $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on every
vector: for every $v\in M$ and every $i$ there are integers $N_e(v,i),N_f(v,i)\ge1$
with $E_i^{N_e(v,i)}v=0$ and $F_i^{N_f(v,i)}v=0$. The exponents may depend on
the vector and on $i$, and both directions are required independently;
integrability is not a uniform nilpotence condition.

The following are additional hypotheses, never part of the definition:
finiteness of the dimension of every $M_\mu$; boundedness of the set of $\mu$
with $M_\mu\ne0$ above (or below); finite generation of $M$. The zero module is
a $P$-graded type-one weight module with the empty grading ($M_\mu=0$ for all
$\mu$), and it is integrable.

Two remarks are recorded here and proved below. First, when the pairing
separates $P$, the spaces $M_\mu$ are exactly the simultaneous eigenspaces of
the $K_h$, and the present definition recovers the usual type-one weight
modules (Verification, steps 2.1 and 4.1). Second, when the pairing does not
separate, distinct labels $\mu\ne\mu'$ may carry the same toral character, and
a simultaneous toral eigenspace must not be equated with a single label space;
the definition therefore takes the label grading as data. The regularization of
finite-cone support and all highest-weight comparisons on this page are proved
later, not assumed here by writing $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$.
No choice principle enters this definition.
items.strategy: This is a definition of the explicit label grading needed for the broad published pairing. Each vector has finite support in the direct sum. The integer pairing gives the toral eigenvalues; generator degree compatibility is required as data and is not inferred from distinct eigencharacters when the pairing has kernel. Local nilpotence is imposed separately. The standard spectral category is recovered exactly when the torus characters separate the labels.

items.title: The contravariant form on an integrable highest weight module
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The **linear
contravariant anti-involution** $\sigma$ of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is defined on
generators by

$$\sigma(q)=q,\qquad\sigma(K_h)=K_h,\qquad\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1},\qquad\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i,$$

extended as an anti-algebra map, $\sigma(xy)=\sigma(y)\sigma(x)$. It is
$\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, preserves the torus (it does not invert it), and is an
involution (Verification, step 1.1). It is distinct from the semilinear
contravariant anti-involution $\tau$ with $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$,
$\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
so $\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ for all $i$, and let $(M,v_\lambda)$ be a
**normalized highest weight module**: $M$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum
weight module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) with
$v_\lambda\in M_\lambda$, $E_iv_\lambda=0$ for all $i$, and $M=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.
(The normalized simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$ is the companion
construction later on this page; the present definition applies to any
normalized highest weight module, in particular to the Verma module and to its
simple quotient.)

A **contravariant form** on $(M,v_\lambda)$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon M\times M\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(i) $B$ is symmetric: $B(u,v)=B(v,u)$ for all $u,v\in M$;

(ii) $B$ is **homogeneous** for the label grading: $B(M_\mu,M_\tau)=0$
whenever the two labels have different toral characters, that is, whenever
$\langle\mu,h\rangle\ne\langle\tau,h\rangle$ for some $h\in P^{\vee}$;

(iii) $B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$ (the normalization);

(iv) $B$ is $\sigma$-invariant: $B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$ for all
$x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)$ and all $u,v\in M$.

Because $\sigma$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear and fixes the torus, condition (iv)
is equivalent to the adjunction displays

$$B(K_hu,v)=B(u,K_hv),\qquad B(E_iu,v)=B(u,q_iF_iK_i^{-1}v),\qquad B(F_iu,v)=B(u,q_i^{-1}K_iE_iv),$$

for all $u,v\in M$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$ (Verification, step 2.1).

For $\lambda$ dominant and $L(\lambda)$ the normalized simple highest weight
module, such a form exists, is unique, and is nondegenerate on $L(\lambda)$;
moreover distinct label-weight spaces with distinct characters are orthogonal
by (ii). Uniqueness is proved here (Verification, step 2.2), as is the
orthogonality; consequently, when the pairing separates $P$, the distinct
label-weight spaces of $L(\lambda)$ are orthogonal and the restriction of $B$
to each finite-dimensional label-weight space is nondegenerate (Verification,
step 4.1). The
existence, the identification of the radical on the Verma module and the
descent to $L(\lambda)$ are proved in the local Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`, which
is the declared justification of this definition. That lemma is proved on this
page, and its statement is the supplier of the existence and nondegeneracy
clauses above; establishing those clauses is its content rather than a claim of
this definition.
items.strategy: This fixes the actual linear anti-involution and normalization. The local Cartan-projection lemma proves existence, uniqueness, symmetry, homogeneity, radical/maximal-submodule identification and descent, with exact source conventions; no standard-arguments existence step is deferred to an author.

items.title: Quantum Verma modules $M(\lambda)$, highest weight vectors, and the simple highest weight quotient $L(\lambda)$
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with Borel subalgebra
$U_q^{\ge0}=U_q^0U_q^+$ and negative half $U_q^-$
([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]). Fix
$\lambda\in P$ and let $\mathbb Q(q)_\lambda=\mathbb Q(q)$ be the
**Borel character module** on which $K_h$ acts by the scalar
$q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}$ and every $E_i$ acts as $0$ (the character is a
well-defined $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism
$\chi_\lambda\colon U_q^{\ge0}\to\mathbb Q(q)$, Verification, step 1.1). The
**quantum Verma module** is the induced module

$$M(\lambda):=U_q(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U_q^{\ge0}}\mathbb Q(q)_\lambda,$$

a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module, with distinguished vector
$v_\lambda:=1\otimes1$ ([[def-quotient-ring]] for the quotient/induction
conventions).

Then (Verification, steps 2.1 and 3.1):

(i) $M(\lambda)$ carries the **canonical $P$-label grading**
$M(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M(\lambda)_\mu$ with
$M(\lambda)_{\lambda-\nu}=U_q^-[-\nu]v_\lambda$ for $\nu\in Q_+$ and
$M(\lambda)_\mu=0$ otherwise; each $M(\lambda)_\mu$ is finite dimensional
(there are only finitely many words in the $F_i$ of a given root degree), and
$M(\lambda)_\lambda=\mathbb Q(q)v_\lambda$ is the highest line. With this
grading $M(\lambda)$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum weight module
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and $v_\lambda$ is a highest
weight vector: $K_hv_\lambda=q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}v_\lambda$,
$E_iv_\lambda=0$, $M(\lambda)=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.

(ii) (Universal property) For every left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $V$ and every
$v\in V$ with $K_hv=q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}v$ and $E_iv=0$ for all $h,i$
there is a unique $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $M(\lambda)\to V$ with
$v_\lambda\mapsto v$; if $V=U_q(\mathfrak g)v$ is cyclic, this map is
surjective. When $V$ is a $P$-graded type-one module and $v\in V_\lambda$, the
map is grading-preserving.

(iii) The sum $N(\lambda)$ of all proper graded submodules of $M(\lambda)$ is a
proper graded submodule, and

$$L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/N(\lambda)$$

is the **simple highest weight quotient**: it has no nonzero proper graded
submodule, and it is the unique simple graded quotient of $M(\lambda)$ up to
isomorphism ([[def-submodule]]). Thus the maximal proper submodule occurring
here is the sum of *all* proper graded submodules, not an arbitrarily chosen
maximal one; no choice is used.

If the pairing separates $P$, then every submodule of $M(\lambda)$ is graded,
$N(\lambda)$ is the unique maximal proper submodule, and $L(\lambda)$ is the
ordinary simple (not only graded-simple) quotient: this is the usual simple
weight-module quotient of the Verma module over a separating torus
(Verification, step 4.1).

The contravariant Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`
identifies $N(\lambda)$ with the radical of the normalized Verma contravariant
form and gives the canonical normalized form on $L(\lambda)$; for $\lambda$
dominant integral, the existence theorem
`thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique` proves the
ordinary simplicity and the universal integrable conclusions. Both are
declared obligations of those later items, not assumptions here.
items.strategy: The one-dimensional Borel character respects its defining relations. Triangular decomposition identifies the induced vector space with U_q^- and gives its chosen lambda-Q_+ grading. Independent simple-root labels give a unique nu for each lambda-nu. Fixed height has finitely many words since I is finite, so every component is finite dimensional without a PBW basis choice. Induction of the given Borel vector proves the degree-preserving universal property. A proper graded submodule has zero lambda-component: containing a nonzero top vector would generate M. The sum of such submodules still has zero top component because every vector is a finite sum of vectors from them. Therefore it is proper. Any proper graded submodule of L lifts to a proper submodule of M containing N and hence equals N, proving graded simplicity. A simple graded quotient has a maximal graded kernel; the sum N contains that kernel and is proper, so maximality forces equality. This fixes the native reversed containment. The local contravariant-form lemma gives a concrete radical description, and the integrable/local-specialization suppliers give the stronger dominant universal conclusions.

items.title: The Lusztig-Kashiwara bilinear form on the negative half: the recursion
items.statement:
Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its skew derivations $e_i'$
([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), and let
$\varepsilon\colon U_q^-\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the **augmentation**, the projection
onto the degree-zero component $U_q^-[0]=\mathbb Q(q)\cdot1$ (so
$\varepsilon(Q)=0$ on all positive-height components and $\varepsilon(1)=1$).

The **normalized Lusztig–Kashiwara form** on $U_q^-$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon U_q^-\times U_q^-\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(H) $B$ is **homogeneous**: $B\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu]\bigr)=0$ whenever
$\nu\ne\mu$;

(N) $B(1,1)=1$;

(R) $B(F_iP,Q)=B(P,e_i'Q)$ for all $i\in I$ and all $P,Q\in U_q^-$.

Equivalently, axioms (H) and (N) may be replaced by the single **counit
normalization**

(C) $B(1,Q)=\varepsilon(Q)$ for all $Q\in U_q^-$,

in the presence of (R) (Verification, step 1.1).

Axioms (H) and (N) (equivalently (C)) are essential and not redundant: the
recursion (R) together with $B(1,1)=1$ alone neither forces symmetry nor
uniqueness, as the rank-one witness of step 2.2 shows.

The axioms determine $B$ uniquely: peeling first letters in the first argument
writes every positive-height $P$ as a finite sum $P=\sum_iF_iP_i$ and evaluates
$B(P,Q)=\sum_iB(P_i,e_i'Q)$, reducing the height; the base of the induction is
(C) (Verification, step 2.1). The **existence, symmetry and nondegeneracy** of
$B$ on $U_q^-$ for the actual quotient by the Serre ideal are not proved here:
they are the content of the negative-half form theorem
`thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral`,
the declared justification of this definition, which also settles the exact
integrality normalization ($A$-valuedness on the word lattice and the
Gaussian-factorial denominators on the divided-power lattice). That theorem
is proved on this page, and its statement is the declared supplier of
existence, symmetry and nondegeneracy; this definition itself claims only that
(H), (N) and (R) determine $B$ and that the normalization cannot be relaxed.
items.strategy: Because the zero component is Q(q)1, homogeneity and B(1,1)=1 give B(1,Q)=epsilon(Q). Every positive-height word has a first letter. The adjunction removes that letter and applies e_i' to the second argument, so height induction fixes every value and proves uniqueness without assuming symmetry. The form theorem establishes that these forced values descend through the Serre ideal and are symmetric/nondegenerate. Do not transpose an arbitrary recursively defined form before imposing homogeneity.

items.title: Divided-power multiplication, toral binomials and the $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ reordering identity
items.statement:
Let $i\in I$ and let $T_{i,c,t}$ be the toral quantum binomials of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]
($i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$, $t\ge0$, $T_{i,c,0}=1$), inside the Drinfeld–Jimbo
algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]
with $U_A$ and its parts $U_A^-,U_A^0,U_A^+$ as in that definition. Write
$E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $E^{(a)}=E_i^{(a)}$, $F^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}$ for the divided
powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] and put
$q=q_i$ inside the displayed formulas.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)},\qquad F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}.$$

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** For $t\ge1$,
$$T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{\,t}-q_i^{\,-t}}\,T_{i,c,t-1}.$$
Each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb Q(q)$; the toral elements commute with one another and with all $K_h$.
For all $i,j$ and all $m\in\mathbb Z$ one has
$K_i^{\,m}T_{j,c,t}=T_{j,c,t}K_i^{\,m}$ if $i\ne j$, while
$E_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-2,t}E_i$, $E_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-a_{ij},t}E_j$,
$F_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+2,t}F_i$, $F_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+a_{ij},t}F_j$ for all $j$.
In particular $E_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0E_i$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0F_i$,
$T_{i,c,t}E_i=E_iT_{i,c+2,t}\in E_iU_A^0$ and
$T_{i,c,t}F_i=F_iT_{i,c-2,t}\in F_iU_A^0$: the toral factor can be moved to the
middle at the cost of a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with every coefficient a toral quantum binomial in $U_A^0$. In particular
$E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and
$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$.
For $i\ne j$, $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute; the same-half divided powers
$E_i^{(a)},E_j^{(b)}$ (and likewise $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$) commute whenever
$a_{ij}=0$, and for $a_{ij}\ne0$ no commutation is asserted.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear
combination of products $b_-u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and
$b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module. No
independence of the spanning family is asserted.
items.strategy: Divided-power multiplication is the factorial identity, with Gaussian coefficients in A. The toral product definition gives commutativity and T_{i,c,t}E_j=E_jT_{i,c+a_ij,t}, T_{i,c,t}F_j=F_jT_{i,c-a_ij,t}; the K_h commutations contribute the prescribed Laurent q-powers. To prove E_i^(a)F_i^(b)=Σ_t F_i^(b-t)T_{i,2t-a-b,t}E_i^(a-t), induct on a, with a=0 immediate. Use E_iF_i^(u)=F_i^(u)E_i+F_i^(u-1)T_{i,1-u,1}, the exact published rank-one formula. Multiplying the a-case by E_i gives [a+1]_i E_i^(a+1)F_i^(b). Move E_i past the toral factor, multiply E_iE_i^(a-t)=[a-t+1]_iE_i^(a-t+1), and collect the terms with the same t. Their coefficients agree because [a+1]_i T_{i,2t-a-b-1,t}=[a-t+1]_i T_{i,2t-a-b-2,t}+T_{i,t-b,1}T_{i,2t-a-b-2,t-1}. Verify this finite product identity by putting the two terms over the product denominators of T, canceling their common factors, and applying [u+v]_i=q_i^v[u]_i+q_i^{-u}[v]_i. This argument occurs in Q(q), where [a+1]_i is nonzero; the final formula has coefficients T in U_A^0 and makes no division by a nonunit within U_A. Boundary terms use [0]_i=0 and out-of-range divided powers zero. For i≠j, only the cross halves E_i,F_j commute. To span triangular products, move positive generators right past negative generators using the formula, and move toral factors to the middle with the exact shifts above. Order terms by total positive/negative divided-power height and then number of cross inversions: non-leading t terms reduce height and t=0 terms reduce inversions. The process terminates. Never commute two adjacent-root generators within the same half. Gaussian coefficients lie in A; toral binomial coefficients lie in U_A^0, not in A itself.

items.title: Integral skew-string coefficients on the divided-power negative half
items.statement:
Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its
Kashiwara skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$
([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]), let
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A^-$ be the divided-power half generated by
the $F_i^{(r)}$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ preserves $U_A^-$: $e_i'(U_A^-)\subseteq U_A^-$.

(ii) Define, for $x\in U_q^-$,
$$P_ix:=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^nq_i^{-n(n-1)/2}\,F_i^{(n)}(e_i')^n x,$$
the sum being finite on each $x$ because $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent, and the
powers $(e_i')^n$ being ordinary, not divided, powers of the derivation. Then
$P_i$ is a well-defined $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear map with $e_i'P_i=0$ that fixes
$\ker e_i'$ pointwise and annihilates $F_iU_q^-$; hence
$U_q^-=\ker e_i'\oplus F_iU_q^-$ and $P_i$ is the projection onto $\ker e_i'$
along $F_iU_q^-$.

(iii) Every $x\in U_A^-$ has a unique finite expansion
$$x=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}x_n,\qquad e_i'x_n=0,$$
with $x_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^nx\in U_A^-$ for every $n$; the sum is finite
because $(e_i')^nx=0$ for large $n$. Consequently the string operators
$\tilde e_i\bigl(\sum_nF_i^{(n)}x_n\bigr):=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}x_n$ and
$\tilde f_i\bigl(\sum_nF_i^{(n)}x_n\bigr):=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}x_n$
preserve $U_A^-$.

No global $A$-basis and no freeness of $U_A^-$ over $A$ is assumed or asserted.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** compute $e_i'$ and its powers on divided-power words, use
the resulting explicit q-binomial sum for the projector, and read the
decomposition and the integrality of its coefficients off that computation.

1.1 The deletion rule. From $e_i' F_i=q_i^{-2}F_ie_i'+1$ and $e_i'(1)=0$, induction on $r\ge1$ gives $e_i'(F_i^r)=(\sum_{s=0}^{r-1}q_i^{-2s})F_i^{r-1}=q_i^{-(r-1)}[r]_iF_i^{r-1}$. Dividing by the nonzero $[r]_i!$ yields $e_i'(F_i^{(r)})=q_i^{-(r-1)}F_i^{(r-1)}$. For $j\ne i$, the relation $e_i' F_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'$ and $e_i'(1)=0$ give $e_i'(F_j^r)=0$, hence $e_i'(F_j^{(r)})=0$. [given, F1, F4, algebra]

2.1 $e_i'$ preserves $U_A^-$: by [F3] it suffices to check a divided-power word $w=F_{j_1}^{(r_1)}\cdots F_{j_m}^{(r_m)}$, by induction on $m$ using the twisted Leibniz rule of [F1] and the deletion rule of step 1.1: $e_i'(w)=e_i'(F_{j_1}^{(r_1)})w'+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(F_{j_1}^{(r_1)}),h_i\rangle}F_{j_1}^{(r_1)}e_i'(w')$, where $w'$ is the restricted word, the first factor is $0$ or $q_i^{-(r_1-1)}F_i^{(r_1-1)}\in U_A^-$ by step 1.1, the scalar $q_i^{\langle-r_1\alpha_{j_1},h_i\rangle}=q_i^{-r_1a_{ij_1}}\in A$, and $e_i'(w')\in U_A^-$ by induction; products of divided powers lie in $U_A^-$. By [F1] linearity extends this to all of $U_A^-$. [step 1.1, F1, F3, algebra]

2.2 Powers of the derivation on a string: if $u\in\ker e_i'$ then for $0\le n\le m$, $(e_i')^nF_i^{(m)}u=q_i^{-nm+n(n+1)/2}F_i^{(m-n)}u$. For $n=0$ this is clear; for the induction step, $e_i'(F_i^{(m-n)}u)=e_i'(F_i^{(m-n)})u+q_i^{-2(m-n)}F_i^{(m-n)}e_i'(u)=q_i^{-(m-n-1)}F_i^{(m-n-1)}u$, where the second summand vanishes because $e_i'u=0$; multiplying by $q_i^{-nm+n(n+1)/2}$ gives the exponent $-(n+1)m+(n+1)(n+2)/2$ as required. [step 1.1, F1, algebra]

3.1 The projector: $P_i$ is well defined by [F2], and $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear. Consecutive terms cancel in $e_i'P_i$: applying $e_i'$ to the $n$-th term gives $(-1)^nq_i^{-n(n-1)/2}[e_i'(F_i^{(n)})(e_i')^n+q_i^{-2n}F_i^{(n)}(e_i')^{n+1}]=(-1)^nq_i^{-n(n-1)/2}[q_i^{-(n-1)}F_i^{(n-1)}(e_i')^n+q_i^{-2n}F_i^{(n)}(e_i')^{n+1}]$ by steps 1.1, 2.2, and the contribution of the second part of the $n$-th term cancels the first part of the $(n+1)$-st term because $-n(n-1)/2-2n=-n(n+1)/2-(n)$; the $n=0$ contribution of the second part is $(e_i')^1$ and equals the first part of the $n=1$ term, so $e_i'P_i=0$. If $e_i'x=0$ then $(e_i')^nx=0$ for $n\ge1$, so $P_ix=F_i^{(0)}(e_i')^0x=x$: $P_i$ fixes $\ker e_i'$ pointwise. [step 2.2, given, algebra]

3.2 $P_i$ annihilates $F_i\ker e_i'$: for $u\in\ker e_i'$ and $m\ge1$, step 2.2 gives $(e_i')^n(F_i^{(m)}u)=q_i^{-nm+n(n+1)/2}F_i^{(m-n)}u$ for $n\le m$, and $(e_i')^n(F_i^{(m)}u)=q_i^{-n(m-1)}F_i^{(m-1)}(e_i'u)=0$ for $n>m$ (the surviving term of the Leibniz expansion at the first step where the derivative reaches $u$); hence $P_i(F_i^{(m)}u)=\sum_{n=0}^{m}(-1)^nq_i^{-n(n-1)/2}F_i^{(n)}q_i^{-nm+n(n+1)/2}F_i^{(m-n)}u=\sum_{n=0}^{m}(-1)^nq_i^{-nm+n}\binom{m}{n}_iF_i^{(m)}u=\bigl[\sum_{n=0}^{m}(-1)^nq_i^{-n(m-1)}\binom{m}{n}_i\bigr]F_i^{(m)}u$, using [F4] for $F_i^{(n)}F_i^{(m-n)}$. By [F5] the bracket is $1$ for $m=0$ and $0$ for $m\ge1$; hence $P_i$ fixes $\ker e_i'$ and annihilates $F_i^{(m)}\ker e_i'$ for every $m\ge1$. [step 2.2, F4, F5, algebra]

4.1 Decomposition and uniqueness: for $x\in U_q^-$ let $m$ be maximal with $(e_i')^mx\ne0$ (finite by [F2]) or $m=0$ if $e_i'x=0$, and put $x_m:=q_i^{m(m-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^mx$; then $e_i'x_m=q_i^{m(m-1)/2}e_i'P_i(e_i')^mx=0$ by step 3.1, and $x':=x-F_i^{(m)}x_m$ satisfies $(e_i')^mx'=(e_i')^mx-q_i^{-m(m-1)/2}x_m=0$ by step 2.2 and step 3.1, so $\operatorname{ord}(x')\le m-1$. Descending induction on $m$ therefore writes $x=\sum_{n}F_i^{(n)}x_n$ with $e_i'x_n=0$ and $x_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^nx$: at each stage the coefficient of the remainder agrees with the claimed formula because $P_i$ annihilates the subtracted strings $F_i^{(m-n)}x_m$ by step 3.2, so $P_i(e_i')^nx'=P_i(e_i')^nx$ for $n<m$. If also $x=\sum_nF_i^{(n)}y_n$ with $e_i' y_n=0$, subtract the two finite expansions and put $z_n:=x_n-y_n$. If some $z_n$ is nonzero, let $N$ be its largest index. Applying $(e_i')^N$ to $0=\sum_nF_i^{(n)}z_n$ gives $0=q_i^{-N(N-1)/2}z_N$ by step 2.2, a contradiction. Thus every $z_n=0$, proving uniqueness. [step 2.2, step 3.1, step 3.2, F2, algebra]

5.1 Integrality and conclusion: each $x_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^nx$ lies in $U_A^-$, because $e_i'$ preserves $U_A^-$ by step 2.1, every $(e_i')^nx$ is therefore in $U_A^-$, the coefficients $q_i^{\pm m(m-1)/2}$ and $(-1)^m$ lie in $A$, and each $F_i^{(m)}$ is a generator of $U_A^-$; hence the finite sum $P_i(\,\cdot\,)$ of the definition lies in $U_A^-$ on $U_A^-$. Consequently every string coefficient $x_n$ of an $x\in U_A^-$ is integral. For the projection claim, apply step 4.1 to the expansion of an arbitrary $y$: $F_iy=\sum_{n\ge1}[n]_iF_i^{(n)}y_{n-1}$ decomposes with all string coefficients in $\ker e_i'$ and zero $n=0$ coefficient, so $P_i(F_iy)=0$ by the formula; hence $U_q^-=\ker e_i'\oplus F_iU_q^-$ with $P_i$ the projection along $F_iU_q^-$, and $x_0=P_ix\in U_A^-$ whenever $x\in U_A^-$. Finally the string operators of (iii) are well defined by the uniqueness of the expansion, and they preserve $U_A^-$ because they only shift the divided-power labels $n\mapsto n\pm1$ of the integral coefficients $x_n\in U_A^-$. No global $A$-basis and no freeness of $U_A^-$ was used anywhere. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, F2, F3, algebra] ∎

items.title: Finite-support regularization of quantum label-weight modules
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let $M$ be a
$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) whose support is contained in
a finite union of cones,

$$\operatorname{supp}M\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{s}(\lambda_j-Q_+)\qquad(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_s\in P),$$

where $Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Choose a finite free direct
coordinate summand $X_f\subseteq P$ (with respect to a free basis of $P$,
[[def-free-abelian-group]]) containing all $\lambda_j$ and all $\alpha_i$, and
set

$$Y_{\mathrm{aux}}:=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb ZH_i\Bigr)\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z),\qquad X_{\mathrm{aux}}:=\operatorname{Hom}(Y_{\mathrm{aux}},\mathbb Z),$$

with the evaluation pairing $X_{\mathrm{aux}}\times Y_{\mathrm{aux}}\to\mathbb Z$.
Define $j\colon X_f\to X_{\mathrm{aux}}$ by $j(x)(H_i):=\langle x,h_i\rangle$ and
$j(x)(f):=f(x)$ for $f\in\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z)$, and put
$\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}:=j(\alpha_i)$. Then:

(i) $(I,A,D,X_{\mathrm{aux}},Y_{\mathrm{aux}},q)$ with the simple roots
$\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$ and simple coroots $H_i$ is a symmetrizable Cartan
datum for a quantum group with the same generalized Cartan matrix $A$ and the
same symmetrizer $D$; its pairing is perfect, the $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$ are
linearly independent, the $H_i$ are primitive and independent, and integral
fundamental weights $\Lambda_j$ ($\Lambda_j(H_i)=\delta_{ij}$) exist. Here
$\langle\alpha_j^{\mathrm{aux}},H_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ is the original convention
([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]],
[[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]).

(ii) $M$ carries a unique structure of $X_{\mathrm{aux}}$-graded type-one
quantum weight module for the auxiliary datum with
$\operatorname{supp}M^{\mathrm{aux}}\subseteq j(X_f)$, namely
$$M^{\mathrm{aux}}_{j(x)}:=M_x\quad(x\in X_f),\qquad M^{\mathrm{aux}}_{\xi}:=0\quad(\xi\notin j(X_f)),$$
$$K_{(n,f)}\ \text{acts on}\ M_x\ \text{by}\ q^{\sum_in_i\langle x,h_i\rangle+f(x)}\qquad\bigl((n,f)\in\textstyle\bigoplus_i\mathbb ZH_i\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z)\bigr),$$
with the actions of $E_i$, $F_i$ and of the simple coroots
$K_{d_iH_i}$ unchanged. In particular the old $K_h$ action is recovered from
the label $x$ as $q^{\langle x,h\rangle}$, and the old and auxiliary $E_i,F_i$
actions agree.

(iii) The two recipes are inverse on objects and grading-preserving morphisms:
on $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules with labels in $X_f$ and support as above, the
identity on underlying vector spaces is an equivalence between the category of
$P$-graded type-one modules and the corresponding full subcategory of
$X_{\mathrm{aux}}$-graded type-one modules with labels in $j(X_f)$. This is not
an embedding of the old torus algebra into the new one and is asserted only
inside this finite-support category.

(iv) The construction applies simultaneously to Verma modules and highest weight
modules (supported in $\lambda-Q_+$) and to finite tensor products of such
modules (labels add), by choosing one $X_f$ containing all participating upper
weights and all simple roots; the tensor-product $E_i,F_i$ formulas of [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]] are unchanged because only the diagonal toral characters change.

(v) Rationally, $h_{\mathrm{aux}}:=Y_{\mathrm{aux}}\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$
decomposes as $h_{\mathrm{aux}}=H_{\min}\oplus Z$, where $H_{\min}$ is a
minimal realization of $A$ (of dimension $2n-r$, $n=|I|$, $r=\operatorname{rank}A$)
and $Z\subseteq\ker\alpha$ is a complement on which all $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$
vanish, so the elements of $Z$ are central in the correspondingly extended
Kac–Moody algebra; hence the classical Cartan and multiplicity comparisons of
[[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]] apply to
$H_{\min}$.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** build the auxiliary finite-rank datum by dualizing a finite coordinate summand of $P$, transport the grading and the toral action labelwise, verify the defining relations of the auxiliary datum, and finish with the rational minimal-realization decomposition.

1.1 Choosing a free basis $e_1,\dots$ of $P$, let $S$ be the finite set of basis elements occurring in the finitely many elements $\lambda_j,\alpha_i$, and put $X_f:=\bigoplus_{s\in S}\mathbb Ze_s$. Then $X_f$ is free of finite rank, contains all $\lambda_j$ and $\alpha_i$, and $P=X_f\oplus X_f'$ for the summand $X_f'$ spanned by the remaining basis elements, by [F1]. Consequently $X_f$ contains the whole support of $M$: every weight is some $\lambda_j-\nu$ with $\nu\in\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$ by [F4], and both $\lambda_j$ and the $\alpha_i$ lie in $X_f$. [given, F1, F4, construct]

2.1 By [F2] the evaluation pairing $X_{\mathrm{aux}}\times Y_{\mathrm{aux}}$ is perfect, and the map $j$ is an isomorphism of $X_f$ onto the subgroup $\{j(x)\}$ of $X_{\mathrm{aux}}$; hence $j$ is injective, so the $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}=j(\alpha_i)$ are linearly independent (as the $\alpha_i$ are, [[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]). The $H_i$ are basis elements of the first summand, hence independent and primitive. For all $i,j$, $\langle\alpha_j^{\mathrm{aux}},H_i\rangle=j(\alpha_j)(H_i)=\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ by the row convention of the datum, and $j(\alpha_j)(f)=f(\alpha_j)$ on the second summand; hence the generalized Cartan matrix of the auxiliary datum is $A$ and the symmetrizer $D$ still satisfies $d_ia_{ij}=d_ja_{ji}$. The elements $\Lambda_j\in X_{\mathrm{aux}}$ with $\Lambda_j(H_i)=\delta_{ij}$ and $\Lambda_j|_{\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z)}=0$ are well-defined fundamental weights. Thus (i) holds. [step 1.1, F2, algebra]

3.1 Transport of the module: grade $M^{\mathrm{aux}}$ by $X_{\mathrm{aux}}$ as in (ii) and let $K_{(n,f)}$ act on $M_x$ by the scalar $q^{\sum_in_i\langle x,h_i\rangle+f(x)}$, while $E_i,F_i$ act as before. This is well defined because $P=X_f\oplus X_f'$ and $M$ has no labels in $X_f'$ by step 1.1, so $M=\bigoplus_{x\in X_f}M_x$. The toral relations hold because the scalars multiply ($q^{a}q^{b}=q^{a+b}$ and $K_{(0,0)}$ acts by $1$). For the toral-action relations, $K_{(n,f)}E_jK_{(n,f)}^{-1}$ acts on $M_x$ by $q^{\sum_in_i\langle x+\alpha_j,h_i\rangle+f(x+\alpha_j)-\sum_in_i\langle x,h_i\rangle-f(x)}=q^{\sum_in_i\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle+f(\alpha_j)}=q^{\langle\alpha_j^{\mathrm{aux}},(n,f)\rangle}$, which is the required scalar; the $F_j$-variant has the opposite sign. The mixed relation holds because its toral part involves only $K_{d_iH_i}$, which acts on $M_x$ by $q^{d_i\langle x,H_i\rangle}=q_i^{\langle x,h_i\rangle}$, the same scalar as the original $K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$; and both $E_i,F_i$ coincide with their original actions. The Serre relations hold because they involve only the unchanged $E_i,F_i$ and the unchanged Cartan matrix and $d_i$. Hence $M^{\mathrm{aux}}$ is a type-one module for the auxiliary datum with support in $j(X_f)$. [step 2.1, F3, F4, algebra]

4.1 Converse and equivalence: given an $X_{\mathrm{aux}}$-graded type-one module $N$ with labels in $j(X_f)$ (i.e. $N_\xi=0$ for $\xi\notin j(X_f)$), define $N^{\mathrm{old}}$ with the same underlying vector spaces and $N^{\mathrm{old}}_x:=N_{j(x)}$ for $x\in X_f$; the actions of $E_i,F_i$ are kept, and $K_h$ acts on $N^{\mathrm{old}}_x$ by $q^{\langle j(x),h\rangle}$ where $\langle j(x),h\rangle:=\langle x,h\rangle$ — well defined since $j$ is injective by step 2.1. These two assignments are inverse on objects; on morphisms both are the identity map on underlying $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear maps, and a map preserving one grading preserves the other because $j$ is a bijection $X_f\to j(X_f)$ fixing the $E_i,F_i$ actions. This proves (iii). The construction is not an algebra embedding of tori: $\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z)$ may be nonzero, and its elements act as new labels with no preimage in $P$; the equivalence is only between the stated module categories with labels in $j(X_f)$. [step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Simultaneity: for a Verma module or highest weight module of highest weight $\lambda$ the support lies in $\lambda-Q_+$, and for a finite tensor product of such modules the labels are sums of labels, hence lie in $\sum_k(\lambda^{(k)}-Q_+)\subseteq(\sum_k\lambda^{(k)})-Q_+$; therefore one finite set $\{\lambda_j\}$ (the participating upper weights) and one $X_f$ containing them and all $\alpha_i$ cover all modules under consideration. Under the coproduct the $E_i$- and $F_i$-components are unchanged ($\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$ and $\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$ of [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]), and the toral factors act by the auxiliary characters on both tensor factors, so the auxiliary structure on a tensor product is the tensor product of the auxiliary structures; the collection of such constructions is therefore compatible. This proves (iv). [step 3.1, step 4.1, F3, algebra]

6.1 Rational decomposition: let $h_{\mathrm{aux}}=Y_{\mathrm{aux}}\otimes\mathbb Q$, so $\dim h_{\mathrm{aux}}=n+\operatorname{rank}X_f$, and let $\alpha\colon h_{\mathrm{aux}}\to\mathbb Q^I$ be the evaluation $\alpha(y)_i=\langle\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}},y\rangle$. It is surjective because the $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$ are linearly independent and the pairing is perfect; its restriction to $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}\{H_i\}$ has rank $r=\operatorname{rank}A$ (the matrix $(\langle\alpha_j,H_i\rangle)=(a_{ij})$). Choose $n-r$ rational directions in $h_{\mathrm{aux}}$ whose images under $\alpha$ supplement the image of $\operatorname{span}\{H_i\}$, and let $H_{\min}$ be the span of these directions together with the $n$ independent $H_i$; then $\dim H_{\min}=n+(n-r)=2n-r$ and the coroots $H_i$ together with the chosen directions form a basis of $H_{\min}$ on which $\alpha$ has rank $n$, so $H_{\min}$ is a minimal realization of $A$ in the sense of [[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]] and [[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]. Inside $\ker\alpha$ choose a linear complement $Z$ to $H_{\min}\cap\ker\alpha$; then $h_{\mathrm{aux}}=H_{\min}\oplus Z$ by construction, and $\alpha|_Z=0$, so all simple roots vanish on $Z$ and the corresponding generators are central. This proves (v) and completes the construction. [step 2.1, step 5.1, F2, algebra] ∎

items.title: The bar involution and the contravariant anti-involution preserve $U_A$
items.statement:
Let $\psi$ (the bar involution) and $\tau$ (the contravariant anti-involution) be
the semilinear maps of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]], so
that $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$
and $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$, $\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$,
with $\tau$ anti-multiplicative. Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A$ be
the Lusztig divided-power integral form with its generators $E_i^{(r)}$,
$F_i^{(r)}$, $K_h^{\pm1}$ and toral binomials $T_{i,c,t}$
([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]). Then $\psi(U_A)=U_A$ and
$\tau(U_A)=U_A$. Explicitly, on the generators,

$$\psi(E_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)},\quad \psi(F_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)},\quad \psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1},\quad \psi(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t},$$

$$\tau(E_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)},\quad \tau(F_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)},\quad \tau(K_h)=K_h^{-1},\quad \tau(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t}.$$

In particular both maps restrict to bijections of $U_A$: $\psi$ to a semilinear
algebra involution of $U_A$ and $\tau$ to a semilinear anti-involution of
$U_A$, while $q^{\pm1}\in A$ keeps all coefficients in $A$. These are the two
involutions under which the bar lattice and the contravariant duality of the
later constructions are taken; neither formula is the Chevalley involution
$\omega$, which changes signs, exchanges the two halves and is treated in
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
No choice is used.
items.strategy: Check the assertions on generators. The field involution $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ preserves $A$ and, by [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]], fixes every $[r]_i$ and every $[r]_i!$; hence it fixes each divided power $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ built from a generator fixed by the map. For $\tau$, which is anti-multiplicative, $\tau(E_i^{(r)})=\tau(E_i)^r/\tau([r]_i!)=F_i^r/[r]_i!=F_i^{(r)}$, and symmetrically; on the torus $\tau(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$ and $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$. For a toral binomial, $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ and $K_i\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ replace each factor of $T_{i,c,t}$ by its negative numerator over its negative denominator, hence fix it; the factors commute, so the product is fixed. Thus each of $\psi,\tau$ maps every generator of $U_A$ to an element of $U_A$, and since they are (anti-)algebra maps and preserve the coefficient ring, each maps $U_A$ into itself; both are involutions by [[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]], so the inclusions are equalities. No choice is used.

items.title: Cartan projection constructs the Verma contravariant form and identifies its radical
items.statement:
Let $\lambda\in P$, let $M(\lambda)$ be the Verma module with its canonical
$P$-label grading and highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]), and let
$\sigma$ be the linear contravariant anti-involution of
[[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]
($\sigma(K_h)=K_h$, $\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1}$,
$\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$).

(i) **Existence and uniqueness.** Define the $\lambda$-weight functional
$\eta\colon U_q(\mathfrak g)\to\mathbb Q(q)$ by $\eta(y):=$ the coefficient of
$v_\lambda$ in $yv_\lambda$ (so $\eta(y)$ is unchanged by adding an element of
the Verma ideal $J(\lambda)$, and $\eta(1)=1$). Then
$$B\bigl(av_\lambda,bv_\lambda\bigr):=\eta\bigl(\sigma(a)b\bigr)\qquad(a,b\in U_q^-)$$
is a well-defined bilinear form on $M(\lambda)$; it is homogeneous, normalized
($B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$) and $\sigma$-contravariant,
$B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$. It is the unique such form on $M(\lambda)$, in the
sense of [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]].

(ii) **Radical and descent.** The radical
$\operatorname{rad}B=\{u:B(u,M(\lambda))=0\}$ equals the sum $N(\lambda)$ of all
proper graded submodules of $M(\lambda)$; consequently $B$ descends to a
nondegenerate normalized $\sigma$-contravariant form on the simple highest
weight quotient $L(\lambda)=M(\lambda)/N(\lambda)$.

(iii) **Rank-one norms and dominant singular vectors.** If
$m_i=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ (that is, $\lambda$ dominant), then for
every $r\ge0$
$$B\bigl(F_i^{(r)}v_\lambda,F_i^{(r)}v_\lambda\bigr)=q_i^{\,r(m_i-r)}\binom{m_i}{r}_i,$$
with the Gaussian binomial interpreted as $0$ for $r>m_i$; in particular each
$F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$ lies in the radical, so $B$ factors through the Serre
quotient $M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$. (The same
computation proves the norm formula for every $\lambda$ and all $r$ for which
the right-hand side is read with $m_i=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle$.)

(iv) **Ordinary simplicity.** Let $V$ be an integrable cyclic graded quotient of
$M(\lambda)$ with support in $\lambda-Q_+$ on which the descended form is
nondegenerate. Then $V$ is simple as an ordinary module (not only as a graded
module).

(v) **Integrality of the lattice values.** If $\lambda$ is integral and
$V_A:=U_Av_\lambda=U_A^-v_\lambda\subseteq L(\lambda)$ is the highest lattice of
the Lusztig form ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), then
$B(V_A,V_A)\subseteq A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. No perfectness of $B$ over $A$ is
asserted.
items.strategy: The sigma assignments are a linear anti-involution: check the toral conjugation and mixed commutator directly; sigma(E_iF_i-F_iE_i)=E_iF_i-F_iE_i because the K factors cancel. In each same-half Serre sum, moving its K factors to one side gives the opposite-half Serre sum times a common nonzero toral/scalar factor; symmetry d_i a_ij=d_j a_ji makes the factor independent of the summation index. Applying sigma twice to each generator is identity. Define pr by discarding every triangular summand with a nontrivial positive or negative factor. Set B on the free U^- Verma realization by the formula. To check contravariance on actual cosets, let J be the Verma left ideal generated by E_i and K_h-q^{<lambda,h>}. In chi_lambda pr, terms in U J vanish because E_i at the right leaves positive height and the toral character annihilates the toral generator; terms in sigma(J)U vanish because sigma(E_i) begins with a negative factor and the toral generators are fixed. Thus the formula is balanced through the Verma quotient and B(xu,v)=B(u,sigma(x)v). Also pr sigma=pr: sigma reverses and exchanges the two nontrivial triangular factors, so it preserves which terms have a toral-only component and fixes that component. This proves symmetry. Unequal negative root labels cannot give toral degree zero, proving homogeneity. The top normalization is1. First-letter adjunction proves uniqueness. The radical is a graded submodule by contravariance and symmetry and misses the top. Conversely for a proper graded submodule N and n∈N_{lambda-nu}, pair against every b v_lambda of that degree. The element sigma(b)n belongs to N_lambda=0, so B(n,bv_lambda)=0. Hence N lies in the radical, identifying the radical exactly with N(lambda) and proving nondegenerate descent to L. Each divided singular vector F_i^(m_i+1)v_lambda is killed by every E_j by the rank-one string formula and cross-half commutation; pairing it against every word of its degree gives zero, so it lies in the radical. For the string norm, sigma(F_i^r)=q_i^{-r^2}K_i^rE_i^r; apply the rank-one E_i^rF_i^(r) formula and divide by [r]_i! to obtain q_i^{r(m_i-r)}binom(m_i,r)_i. Finally, in a nonzero ordinary submodule of an integrable graded L choose a nonzero vector and one of its maximum-height homogeneous components x. Nondegeneracy supplies a word b of the same root label with B(x,bv_lambda)≠0. Applying sigma(b) to the vector raises x to a nonzero scalar top vector; components of lesser height, or different labels at the same height, have zero resulting label outside lambda-Q_+. This puts v_lambda in the ordinary submodule, proving ordinary simplicity without assuming that submodule is graded. For the lattice claim, sigma(F_i^(r))=q_i^{-r^2}K_i^rE_i^(r) and sigma(E_i^(r))=q_i^{r^2}F_i^(r)K_i^{-r}, while sigma fixes K_h and all toral binomials, so sigma preserves U_A. The reordering lemma proves pr(U_A)⊂U_A^0. The highest character sends T_{i,c,t} to the integer Gaussian [<lambda,h_i>+c choose t]_i∈A, including negative upper integers by the finite product/negative Gaussian identity. Thus chi_lambda pr(sigma(a)b)∈A for a,b∈U_A^-, proving integral module-form values without any integral-basis or perfectness assumption.

items.title: The dominant quantum Serre quotient is nonzero and integrable
items.statement:
Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral, so $m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$
for all $i$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the Verma module with highest vector
$v_\lambda$ ([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]).
Put $s_i:=F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$.

(i) Every $s_i$ is a singular (highest weight) vector of weight
$\lambda-(m_i+1)\alpha_i$.

(ii) The graded submodule
$S:=\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)s_i=\sum_iU_q^-s_i$ is proper, and the quotient
$\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/S$ is nonzero, has finite-dimensional
label-weight spaces, and is integrable ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]).

(iii) Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of highest weight
$\lambda$ is a quotient of $\tilde L(\lambda)$.

No commutation between divided powers $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$ of distinct indices
with $a_{ij}\ne0$ is assumed anywhere.
items.strategy: The rank-one formula E_iF_i^(t)v=[m_i-t+1]_iF_i^(t-1)v kills s_i at t=m_i+1. For j≠i use cross-half E_jF_i=F_iE_j, so every s_i is singular. Its generated submodule is U_q^-s_i with support lambda-(m_i+1)alpha_i-Q_+, hence has no top component; their sum is proper. The quotient has finite graded pieces as a quotient of the finitely many word spans in M. Every E_i is locally nilpotent by the lambda-Q_+ support bound. For F_i, induct on the length of a word w. The empty word is killed by F_i^(m_i+1). If w=F_iw', increase the already-known exponent. If w=F_jw', j≠i, put N=1-a_ij. The monic quantum Serre relation solves F_i^N F_j as a finite combination of F_i^{N-r}F_jF_i^r, 1≤r≤N. Induct on the left exponent to rewrite F_i^R F_j for R≥N as a linear combination of F_i^tF_jF_i^{R-t}, 0≤t≤N-1. Thus if F_i^S w'v=0, every term vanishes when R≥S+N-1. This proves local F_i nilpotence without the false pairwise-commutation argument. Finally, if an integrable highest vector is killed first by F_i^t, apply E_i to F_i^t v: its coefficient is [t]_i[m_i-t+1]_i and F_i^{t-1}v≠0. Since [t]_i≠0 and q is indeterminate, t=m_i+1. Hence the Verma map to any such cyclic module kills all s_i and factors through tilde L. This is a finite induction and is choice-free.

items.title: Separation of the negative half by iterated skew derivations
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum with
$a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]),
let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), and let
$e_i',e_i''$ be the skew derivations of
[[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]].

(i) **One step.** If $x\in U_q^-[-\nu]$ with $\nu\ne0$ satisfies
$e_i'(x)=0$ for all $i\in I$, then $x=0$.

(ii) **Iterated separation.** For every $0\ne x\in U_q^-[-\nu]$ there is a
sequence $i_1,\dots,i_k\in I$ with $\nu=\alpha_{i_1}+\cdots+\alpha_{i_k}$ (the
multiset is uniquely determined by $\nu$, because the simple roots freely
generate $Q$, and $k=\operatorname{ht}(\nu)$) such that
$e_{i_k}'\cdots e_{i_2}'e_{i_1}'(x)\ne0$. Here the composite is read with the
rightmost factor applied first, so the first chosen derivation $e_{i_1}'$ acts
first; equivalently, the common kernel, on $U_q^-[-\nu]$, of all composites
$e_{i_1}'\cdots e_{i_k}'$ over all such sequences is zero.

The same statements hold with $e_i''$ in place of $e_i'$. This separation property is used by the crystal development and the categorification pairing.

In degree nu=Σ_i n_i alpha_i, multiply its positive-negative pairing by c_nu=∏_i(q_i-q_i^-1)^{n_i} and identify the two generator-word presentations E_i↔F_i. This color-multiplicative scaling gives a form B on the actual Serre quotient, with generator value1 and no radical; c_nu is a nonzero field scalar, so nondegeneracy remains. Its value on two free words is the sum over label-matching permutations of the product of factors q^{-(alpha_i,alpha_j)} at their inversions. Inverting a matching permutation gives the same inversion pairs with their symmetric Cartan products d_i a_ij=d_j a_ji; hence B is symmetric. Separate the possible matches of the first letter of the first word: matching it to position t of the second word contributes the product q_i^{-a_i,j_s} over its preceding letters. This is exactly the deletion formula for e_i', so B(F_iP,Q)=B(P,e_i'Q). Empty words and unequal color degrees give the normalized counit/homogeneity values. Thus the complete auxiliary homogeneous form exists on the Serre quotient and is nondegenerate, using AC only through the published generic pairing supplier. If a positive-degree x is killed by every e_i', its pairing with every first-letter word F_iP is zero; all words of that degree have a first letter, so nondegeneracy gives x=0. For a nonzero x choose one nonzero e_i' image and repeat at strictly decreasing height. After ht(nu) steps the result is a nonzero scalar. State the composite in the actual application order (first chosen derivation acts first, hence is the rightmost factor in the written operator product). The bar gives the same result for e_i''. items.title: The unmodified integral torus has a quantum-binomial basis
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), put
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ ([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]), let
$L:=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbb Z(d_ih_i)\subseteq P^{\vee}$, and let $U_A^0$ be the
$A$-subalgebra of $U_q^0$ generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the toral quantum
binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]).

(a) **One simple torus.** Fix $i\in I$ and write $z:=q_i$, $K:=K_i$,
$T_t:=T_{i,0,t}$ for $t\ge0$. Then for all $r,s\ge0$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and
$t\ge1$,
$$T_rT_s=\sum_{j=0}^{\min(r,s)}z^{rs}K^{-j}\binom{r+s-j}{r}_z\binom{r}{j}_zT_{r+s-j},\qquad T_{c+1,t}=z^tT_{c,t}+K^{-1}z^{-c+t-1}T_{c,t-1},$$
where $\binom{m}{r}_z$ is the Gaussian binomial of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]; all
coefficients lie in $A$. Moreover the $A$-subalgebra of $U_q^0$ generated by
$K^{\pm1}$ and all $T_{c,t}$ equals the $A$-span of
$\{K^{\delta}T_t:\delta\in\{0,1\},\,t\ge0\}$, and that set is an $A$-basis.

(b) **Full torus.** Fix a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $P^{\vee}$, let $J$ be the
finite set of coordinates occurring in the finitely many vectors $d_ih_i$, and
let $D:=\bigoplus_{j\in J}\mathbb Z e_j$ be the corresponding coordinate direct
summand. For every coset of $L$ in $P^{\vee}$ choose the representative $c$
whose $D$-component has minimal sum of coordinate absolute values, ties broken
lexicographically, and whose complementary component is the coset's common
complementary component. Then
$$U_A^0=\bigoplus_{c}K_c\cdot A\text{-span}\Bigl\{\prod_{i\in I}K_i^{\delta_i}T_{i,0,t_i}:\delta_i\in\{0,1\},\,t_i\ge0\Bigr\},$$
the sum over the chosen representatives, so the displayed elements form an
$A$-basis of $U_A^0$.

Both statements are proved directly on the unmodified generators over the
non-PID ring $A$: no integral PBW or canonical-basis input, no inference from
torsion-freeness to freeness, and no modified-${}_A\dot U$ result is used.
items.strategy: For ordinary Gaussian base Q=z², count weighted subsets by the two ordered blocks to prove Vandermonde: [n choose s]_Q=Σ_j Q^{(r-j)(s-j)}[r choose j]_Q[n-r choose s-j]_Q. Multiply by [n choose r]_Q and cancel the finite factorials to replace the product of its three binomials by [r+s-j choose r]_Q[r choose j]_Q[n choose r+s-j]_Q. Translate ordinary Gaussians to symmetric binomials by [a choose b]_z=z^{-b(a-b)}[a choose b]_{z²}. The net coefficient is z^{rs}z^{-jn}. Evaluating T_t at K=z^n gives [n choose t]_z, so the displayed product identity holds at infinitely many K values. A Laurent polynomial over Q(q) with infinitely many roots is zero; hence the identity holds in the actual torus. The product coefficients are Laurent q-powers and integral Gaussian polynomials. The shift identity follows from the finite toral product and quantum Pascal, and its z^t coefficient is an A-unit; First induct on t, with T_{c,0}=1 for every c. If every lower-t shifted binomial is in the span, iterate T_{c+1,t}=z^tT_{c,t}+K^-1z^{-c+t-1}T_{c,t-1} upward from c=0 for positive c. For negative c solve the same equation as T_{c,t}=z^-tT_{c+1,t}−K^-1z^{-c-1}T_{c,t-1}, iterating downward finitely many steps from c=0. All lower-t terms are available by the induction hypothesis and all z powers are A-units. Thus every integer shift lies in the span generated by K± and the T_t. Now M=A-span{T_t,KT_t:t≥0} is stable under K and K^-1: the product recursion yields K^-1 T_t=z^{-2t}KT_t-z^{-t}(z^{t+1}-z^{-t-1})T_{t+1}, K^-1(KT_t)=T_t, K²T_t=z^{2t}T_t+z^t(z^{t+1}-z^{-t-1})KT_{t+1}. Thus each K^mT_t lies in M. The product identity proves M is a subalgebra. It contains1,K,K^-1 and every shifted toral binomial, so it equals the simple toral integral form. For independence over the fraction field, in a finite relation with maximum t=N, KT_N has the unique exponent K^{N+1}; its coefficient is nonzero. Removing it, T_N has the unique exponent K^{-N}. Their coefficients vanish; descending N proves independence. All simple K_i are algebraically independent because d_i h_i are independent in the free lattice and the field torus is Q(q)[Pvee]. Thus tensoring these explicit simple-torus free bases gives the basis over the subgroup L. The group algebra decomposes as the direct sum of K_cQ(q)[L] over cosets. Multiplying integral toral generators only changes the coset and acts within the simple toral subalgebra, so U_A^0 is the direct sum of the corresponding K_c copies of that subalgebra. To choose representatives without a new arbitrary family choice, fix a finite coordinate direct summand of Pvee containing all d_i h_i; choose in each of its cosets the vector of minimal sum of coordinate absolute values, breaking the finite ties lexicographically, and retain all complementary coordinates. This is an explicit representative set. The resulting basis proves freeness over the true non-PID A. Symbolic checks of41 small product/shift/toral-action identities were independent diagnostics; the general Vandermonde and recursion argument is the proof.

items.title: Local q=1 deformation proves integrable highest weight universality
items.statement:
Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight and let
$\tilde L(\lambda)$ be the nonzero integrable quotient of the Verma module
$M(\lambda)$ of [[lem-quantum-highest-weight-serre-quotient-is-integrable]]
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]), with
highest vector $v_\lambda$ and label grading
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]). Put
$R:=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q-1)}\subset\mathbb Q(q)$.

(a) **Character.** Every nonzero graded quotient $V$ of $\tilde L(\lambda)$
whose highest line is nonzero is generated by its highest vector and has in
every label the same dimension as the classical simple integrable highest
weight module of the regularized minimal realization of the same Cartan datum
([[lem-finite-support-regularization-of-quantum-label-weight-modules]],
[[thm-kac-moody-verma-module-has-a-unique-simple-quotient]]); in particular the
character is independent of $V$. No global $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and
no crystal or global basis is used.

(b) **Uniqueness.** Consequently $\tilde L(\lambda)$ is simple, hence is the
canonical simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$, and every integrable cyclic
highest weight module of highest weight $\lambda$ is a quotient of
$L(\lambda)$.

(c) **The $R$-lattice.** For a nonzero highest vector $v$ of $V$, the lattice
$V_R:=\sum_wR\,F_wv$, summed over all ordinary words $w$ in the negative
generators, is stable under every generator of the integral form $U_A$ of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], is finite free over $R$ on each
label weight, and is generated by $v$ under $U_A$ after extension to $R$; its $q=1$ fibre
$V_R/(q-1)V_R$ is the classical simple integrable highest weight module of the
regularized minimal realization. Here the Gaussian binomials
$\binom{m}{r}_i$ of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]
are $R$-valued at integer labels, and the divided-power denominators
$[r]_i!$ and $q_i^{\pm1}$ are $R$-units.
items.strategy: Every nonzero rational function has its integer order at1 times a unit, and an ideal has a least such order, so R is a DVR/PID. Fix such a V. It is integrable by the Serre-quotient lemma. Form V_R as the R-span of ordinary negative words applied to its highest vector. A fixed label weight has finitely many such words, so its lattice is finite generated; it is torsionfree inside the field space and hence free over the actual DVR R. This is not an argument over Z[q±]. The lattice spans each field weight and the top component is exactly Rv, so v survives the fibre. F_i acts integrally. Commute E_i through a negative word; the residual toral coefficients on weight vectors are [<mu,h_i>]_i, Laurent polynomials in R, proving E_i stability. Every divided-power denominator [r]_i! is an R-unit. K_h is a diagonal R-unit, and T_{i,c,t} acts by the regular scalar Gaussian binomial [<mu,h_i>+c choose t]_i; this proves full U_A stability. Local nilpotence identities on any individual lattice vector survive specialization. The specialized E/F/H_i operators satisfy the classical Serre and Cartan relations by the same integral identities, and regularization supplies genuine independent Cartan weights, all old labels and a central character. Its negative words still generate the fibre, whose weight dimensions equal the quantum dimensions by DVR-freeness. Over C the fibre is an integrable finite-weight-space highest module for a finite symmetrizable minimal realization, with finite-cone support. It is simple by the published Casimir suppliers: the Casimir is scalar on a cyclic highest module; a proper nonzero submodule would have a maximal lower weight mu, dominant by rank-one integrability, with the same scalar, contradicting c(lambda)-c(mu)=Σ_i n_i d_i(lambda(h_i)+mu(h_i)+2)>0 when lambda-mu=Σ n_i alpha_i≠0. Thus its character is the classical simple character, independent of V. Apply this to tilde L and its graded simple quotient L; their surjection is between finite-dimensional corresponding weight spaces with identical dimensions, hence is an isomorphism in every weight. This proves universality without global integral bases or a quantum semisimplicity assumption. The same local matrices are rational; characteristic-zero base extension preserves their ranks. The source Berkeley finite-type argument is reproduced weightwise, using the proved classical Casimir comparison in the general case; Lusztig33.1.2 is applied only to the explicitly regularized datum.

items.title: Rational-local quantum halves and torus specialize at q=1
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]), and
$R:=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q-1)}\subset\mathbb Q(q)$, so that $R$ is a DVR with
uniformizer $q-1$ ([[def-discrete-valuation-ring]]). Let
$U_R:=U_A\otimes_AR$ be the base
change of the integral form $U_A$ of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], identified with its image in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

(a) **Halves.** Each root component $U_R^\pm[\pm\nu]$ is a finite free
$R$-module, generated as an $R$-module by ordinary words
$E_{i_1}\cdots E_{i_k}$ (respectively $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$) of degree
$\pm\nu$, and its $q=1$ fibre $U_R^\pm[\pm\nu]\otimes_RR/(q-1)$ is the classical
half $U(\mathfrak n^\pm)_{\mathbb Q}[\pm\nu]$ of the Kac-Moody algebra,
presented by the separate classical Serre relations
([[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]](i),
[[thm-serre-presentation-of-a-kac-moody-algebra]]).

(b) **Torus.** Write $H_i:=T_{i,0,1}$ and let $L=\sum_i\mathbb Z(d_ih_i)$.
Then $U_R^0$ has the $R$-basis
$\{K_c\prod_iK_i^{\delta_i}H_i^{t_i}\}$ with $\delta_i\in\{0,1\}$,
$t_i\ge0$ and $c$ running through the explicit representatives of
$P^{\vee}/L$ of
[[lem-unmodified-integral-torus-has-a-quantum-binomial-basis]](b); and
multiplication
$U_R^-\otimes_RU_R^0\otimes_RU_R^+\to U_R$ is an isomorphism of
$R$-modules.

(c) **Positive quotient.** For every characteristic-zero field $k$ (an
$A$-algebra via $q\mapsto1$), the positive toral quotient
$U_A^0\otimes_Ak/(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$ is the polynomial algebra $k[H_i:i\in I]$
with, in it, $\bar T_{i,c,t}=\binom{H_i+c}{t}$; and the positive full quotient
$(U_A\otimes_Ak)/(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$ is isomorphic to $U(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}})_k$,
where $\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}}$ is the classical Lie algebra presented by the
generators $e_i,f_i,h_i$ with the Cartan and Serre relations, its Cartan being
the span of the independent simple coroots. This is an assertion about the
stated quotient only: it is not claimed that $K_h=1$ in the unquotiented
specialization $U_A\otimes_Ak$, where genuine toral characters such as
$K=-1$ for $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ survive. Direct substitution $q=1$ into the
vanishing denominators $q_i^s-q_i^{-s}$ is never performed.
items.strategy: A nonzero rational function has a unique integer order at q=1 and a unit factor; every ideal of R has a least such order and is generated by that power of q-1, proving the DVR/PID property. R localizes A by inverting nonzero integers and polynomials nonzero at1, so flat localization identifies U_A⊗R with its image. Every [r]_i! has nonzero value r! and is an R-unit; hence U_R^± is generated by ordinary E_i/F_i. Fixed root degree has finitely many words, so its component is finite generated and torsionfree inside the field half and thus R-free. Its rank is the generic half dimension, equal to the classical dimension by the published rank supplier (the declared AC use). Quantum Serre relations specialize and give a surjection from the classical half; equal finite dimensions make it an isomorphism degreewise. For the torus, the integral identity [t]_iT_{i,c,t}=(q_i^{c-t+1}H_i+K_i^-1[c-t+1]_i)T_{i,c,t-1} implies U_R^0 is generated by K_h and H_i, since [t]_i is an R-unit. In the independent simple torus L=Σ_i Z(d_i h_i), its presentation is R[H_i,K_i]/(K_i^2-(q_i-q_i^-1)K_iH_i-1). Each monic quadratic gives a free polynomial-H module with basis K_i^delta_i. It injects in Q(q)[L]: over the fraction field solve H_i=(K_i-K_i^-1)/(q_i-q_i^-1), and the monic presentation is torsionfree over R. Choose a finite coordinate summand of Pvee containing all d_i h_i; in each of its cosets of L choose minimal coordinate absolute-value sum, breaking finite ties lexicographically, and retain the complementary coordinates. This gives explicit coset representatives without an arbitrary family choice. The group algebra decomposes over these cosets, giving the displayed R-basis of the full toral algebra. Triangular spanning is the reordering lemma. All factor modules are now R-free (the halves are direct sums of their finite free components), so their tensor product is torsionfree; field triangular decomposition proves injectivity. At q=1 and K_h=1, the same toral recursion gives t Tbar_{i,c,t}=(H_i+c-t+1)Tbar_{i,c,t-1}, so Tbar=binom(H_i+c,t). The local toral basis/presentation gives no other relation among H_i. Alternatively evaluate the torus on all integral characters phi:Pvee→Z: H_i evaluates to phi(h_i); independence of h_i makes these values contain a full-rank integer subgroup of Z^I, which is Zariski dense in characteristic zero. Thus polynomial independence and the exact toral kernel are proved. The mixed relation gives [E_i,F_j]=δ_ijH_i, and T_{i,0,1}E_j=E_jT_{i,a_ij,1} specializes to [H_i,E_j]=a_ijE_j (similarly F_j). Serre and toral relations therefore give a surjection from the classical derived enveloping algebra. Both algebras have the same negative-toral-positive vector decomposition (classical PBW/Serre and the proved local triangular decomposition), so that map is an isomorphism. The extra classical Cartan directions are reconstructed on graded modules, not falsely added as algebra generators to this positive quotient.

items.title: The negative-half bilinear form is symmetric, nondegenerate and integral
items.statement:
Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), with skew derivations
$e_i',e_i''$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]),
and let $(\ ,\ )$ be a bilinear form on $U_q^-$.

(i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and
$(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ for all $i,P,Q$ exists on $U_q^-$; every normalized
homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; and by the
uniqueness of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]
there is exactly one such form. No separate right-adjunction formula for
$(P,QF_i)$ is asserted: in the rank-one subalgebra a formula
$(P,QF_i)=c\,(e_i''P,Q)$ with constant $c$ is false, as the explicit values in
(iv) show.

(ii) **Orthogonality.** $(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu])=0$ whenever $\nu\ne\mu$.

(iii) **Nondegeneracy.** For every $0\ne x\in U_q^-$ there is $y\in U_q^-$ with
$(x,y)\ne0$; equivalently, the restriction of the form to each
finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[-\nu]$ is nondegenerate.

(iv) **Integrality on the word lattice.** Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]) and let $W\subseteq U_A^-$ be the
$A$-span of the monomials $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$ ($k\ge0$). Then
$W\subseteq U_A^-$ (because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ and $[k]_i!\in A$), and
$(W,W)\subseteq A$. On the larger divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ the form is
*not* $A$-valued: in the rank-one subalgebra generated by a single $F_i$ one
has, for all $a,b\ge0$,
$$(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=\delta_{ab}\frac{q_i^{-a(a-1)/2}}{[a]_i!}=\delta_{ab}\frac{1}{[a]_{q_i^2}!},$$
in particular $(F_i^{(2)},F_i^{(2)})=1/(1+q_i^2)\notin A$; here
$[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{m=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(m-1)})$. Globally, with
$A_{\mathrm{loc}}=A[s^{-1}:s\in S]$, the localization of $A$ inverting the
multiplicative set $S$ generated by $\{[r]_i!:i\in I,r\ge1\}$ (equivalently inverting the
Gaussian factorials $[r]_{q_i^2}!$), one has
$(U_A^-,U_A^-)\subseteq A_{\mathrm{loc}}$: divided-power words are word
vectors divided by finite products of these factorials. This is an exact
denominator bound, not an $A$-integrality assertion on $U_A^-$ in this
normalization.
items.strategy: The separation lemma constructs the form explicitly from the proved generic Hopf pairing by color-degree scaling c_nu=∏(q_i-q_i^-1)^{nu_i}. Its matching-permutation Gram formula proves symmetry and e'-adjunction, and the generic pairing proves descent and nondegeneracy on each actual Serre-quotient component. The form Definition now imposes homogeneity, so uniqueness follows by first-letter peeling. This transport is degree dependent, not one scalar multiplying the whole form. Orthogonality is its homogeneous construction. Alternatively, repeated skew separation and adjunction pair a nonzero x with an appropriate first-letter word; reverse the chosen derivation order correctly when writing that word. For integrality on W, each skew deletion coefficient is a Laurent q-power in A. Height induction therefore gives B(W,W)⊂A. A divided-power word is its underlying ordinary word divided by ∏[r]_i!, giving B(U_A^-,U_A^-)⊂A_loc by bilinearity. In rank one e_i'F_i^(n)=q_i^{-(n-1)}F_i^(n-1). Since F_i^(n)=[n]_i^-1 F_iF_i^(n-1), its squared norm obeys b_n=q_i^{-(n-1)}b_{n-1}/[n]_i, starting b_0=1. Thus b_n=q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}/[n]_i!=1/[n]_{q_i^2}! and different powers are orthogonal. At n=2 this is 1/(1+q_i^2), not in A, proving the exact native correction. No integrality on the whole divided-power lattice is claimed without the stated localization. AC is inherited only from the generic pairing/separation supplier.
