items.title: The q=1 toral specialization identifies the classical Cartan generators
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, let
$U_A$ be the integral form with toral part $U_A^0$
([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]) and let $k$ be a
characteristic-zero field regarded as an $A$-algebra by $q\mapsto1$.
Write $H_i:=T_{i,0,1}$ and $\bar x$ for the image of $x$ in a specialization.

(a) **Algebra level.** The positive toral quotient
$U_A^0\otimes_Ak/(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$ is the polynomial algebra
$k[H_i:i\in I]$, and in it $\bar T_{i,c,t}=\binom{H_i+c}{t}$ for all
$c\in\mathbb Z$, $t\ge0$
([[lem-rational-local-quantum-halves-and-torus-specialize-at-q-one]](c)).
No residual $K_h$-ambiguity remains after this quotient — the ideal
$(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$ is exactly the kernel of the comparison with
$k[H_i]$ — but it is *not* claimed that $K_h=1$ in the unquotiented
specialization $U_A^0\otimes_Ak$.

(b) **Label-graded lattices.** Let $M$ be a $P$-graded type-one
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module with label grading $M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]), and let
$M_A=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}(M_A\cap M_\mu)$ be a $U_A$-stable $A$-submodule that
is graded in the *lattice's own* sense, i.e. it is the direct sum of its
intersections with the label spaces. Then, on $M_A\otimes_Ak$, the operators
induced by $E_i,F_i$ (and all of $U_A$) satisfy: $\bar K_h=\mathrm{id}$ for
every $h\in P^{\vee}$; $\bar T_{i,c,t}$ acts on the image of $M_A\cap M_\mu$ by
the integer $\binom{\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+c}{t}$; and
$[\bar E_i,\bar F_j]=\delta_{ij}\bar H_i$,
$[\bar H_i,\bar E_j]=a_{ij}\bar E_j$,
$[\bar H_i,\bar F_j]=-a_{ij}\bar F_j$, where $\bar H_i$ acts on the image of
$M_A\cap M_\mu$ by the integer $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$.

The grading hypothesis in (b) is a real hypothesis on the lattice: it is not
inferred from the mere fact that $M_A$ spans a weight module. All divisions
that occur are performed inside the DVR
$R=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q-1)}$ (units $[r]_i!$ and $q_i^{\pm1}$); no vanishing
denominator $q_i^s-q_i^{-s}$ is substituted by $q=1$.
items.strategy: The rational-local half/torus theorem proves the algebra-level positive quotient and exact toral kernel using the integral recursion, monic local toral basis and polynomial independence. For lattice operators, diagonal K_h acts by q^{<mu,h>}; the lattice's actual grading ensures this equality applies to a spanning set of lattice vectors and hence specializes to1. The scalar T value is the integer Gaussian [<mu,h_i>+c choose t]_i with q_i=q^{d_i}, not a formula silently dropping d_i. Gaussian integrality gives its q=1 value as the ordinary integer binomial (including negative upper values). The mixed relation gives [E_i,F_j]=δ_ijH_i. The shifted toral identity H_iE_j=E_jT_{i,a_ij,1} and its F version give the remaining classical commutators after the positive quotient, or directly on each lattice weight. No naive division by q_i-q_i^-1 is specialized.

items.title: The integrable quantum highest weight module exists and is unique
items.statement:
Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight, put
$m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the quantum Verma
module with highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]],
[[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

(i) The quotient $\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$
is nonzero, has finite-dimensional label weights and support contained in
$\lambda-Q_+$, is integrable, and equals the canonical simple highest weight
module $L(\lambda)$, which is simple also as an ordinary (not assumed graded)
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module.

(ii) **Universality.** Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of
highest weight $\lambda$ with highest vector $v\ne0$ receives a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $\tilde L(\lambda)\to V$ with
$\bar v_\lambda\mapsto v$, and this map is unique; every nonzero such $V$ is
isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$.

(iii) Its character equals the classical integrable highest weight character of
the explicitly regularized realization of the datum. No global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and no crystal or global basis is used.
items.strategy: Apply the Serre-quotient integrability lemma to construct tilde L, prove nonzero top and local nilpotence, and obtain the universal map to any integrable cyclic highest module. The local q1 deformation lemma compares the finite DVR-free weight lattices in tilde L and its graded simple quotient L with the same classical simple module, giving equal dimensions and hence tilde L=L. The Cartan-projection lemma gives the normalized nondegenerate homogeneous form on L; its maximum-height raising argument proves ordinary simplicity even when an ordinary submodule is not assumed graded. Thus every nonzero quotient in the universal property is the same L. This closes the native gap and does not use a later global Z-basis as an early premise.

items.title: Integrable bounded-above quantum modules with finite-dimensional weight spaces are direct sums of simple highest weight modules
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $M$ be a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module over $\mathbb Q(q)$ for a finite symmetrizable
Cartan datum such that

(a) $M$ is a weight module with $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}M_\mu<\infty$ for every
$\mu\in P$ ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]);

(b) the weight set $\mathrm{wt}(M)$ is bounded above: it is contained in a
finite union $\bigcup_{j=1}^s(\lambda_j-Q_+)$;

(c) $M$ is integrable, i.e. $E_i$ and $F_i$ act locally nilpotently for every
$i$.

Then $M$ is isomorphic to an algebraic direct sum of simple integrable highest
weight modules $L(\lambda)$, $\lambda\in P^+$
([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]);
concretely, every nonzero submodule of $M$ contains a maximal vector $v$ whose
cyclic submodule $U_q(\mathfrak g)v$ is isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$ for some
$\lambda\in P^+$, and $M$ is the direct sum of the submodules generated by the
vectors of any maximal independent family of simple submodules. AC is used
exactly to select a maximal independent family of simple submodules
simultaneously; restricted to any module generated by one finite-dimensional
$U^{\ge0}$-submodule the decomposition is obtained by a finite induction and is
choice-free. The finite-cone modules use the explicit label grading, and the
regularization supplier is used when the original pairing is not separating
([[lem-finite-support-regularization-of-quantum-label-weight-modules]]).
items.strategy: Choose one finite-support regularization for the upper cones; it preserves the grading, all E/F actions and reconstructs the old torus, so prove the statement in the regular support category and transport back. For any vector, U^{≥0}v has finitely many weights: the upper set of each of its finitely many support labels inside the finite union of cones is finite, and each weight has finite dimension. An integrable cyclic highest submodule is the simple L(lambda) by the completed early universality theorem. For restricted duality use the Q(q)-linear anti-involution phi fixing the torus and interchanging E_i,F_i (tau composed with bar), on M^*=⊕_mu Hom(M_mu,Q(q)). Finite-dimensional weights give M=M^{**}. To verify integrability of the dual, each rank-one cyclic submodule in M is finite dimensional: commute its E/F powers into F^bE^a form, and use local nilpotence on the finitely many E^a v. The generic rank-one finite modules split into finite simple strings by their distinct Casimir scalars, with equal highest labels split by the top-vector bases. The finite sum U_iM_mu therefore captures every string contributing to the mu-coordinate and gives a uniform exponent for the transpose arrows into that coordinate; the dual is integrable. Fix a globally maximal weight lambda in a nonzero submodule, a vector v_lambda, and extend its evaluation functional to the full finite-dimensional M_lambda with value1 on v_lambda. This gives phi_lambda∈M^*_lambda (not merely a functional on V). Since no higher label exists, it is highest. Its cyclic W is L(lambda). Dualizing W→M^* gives M→W^*; its restriction to V=U_qv_lambda is nonzero on the top and hence an isomorphism between the simple highest modules. Invert that restriction to obtain a retraction M→V and split. If M=U_qF for finite-dimensional U^{≥0}-stable F, choose a maximal weight of F: it is globally maximal in M because multiplying negative words only lowers the finite weights of F. The retraction reduces the dimension of the generating image of F, giving finite induction. For arbitrary M every cyclic submodule is of that form, so M is a sum of simple submodules. Under AC select a maximal independent family of them (Zorn, or simultaneous singular bases) and prove it spans: a simple submodule not contained in the sum intersects it either in itself or zero, and the latter would enlarge the family. This yields the algebraic direct sum. The normalized sigma-form gives the equivalent self-dual identification; no nonexistent extension from V^* to M^* is asserted without explicitly choosing the functional in M_lambda. The commissioned finite rank-one Casimir/string argument is supplied locally from the published rank-one formulas. Upper-cone root coefficients bound each fixed simple-root line; finite strings bound its bottom, proving restricted-dual integrability without a global coroot bound. A maximal generating label need not dominate all other labels. Use the finite graded hull and finite-simple-sum argument for ordinary ungraded submodules; no prerequisite on the later QG3 page is introduced.

items.title: Specialization at q=1 recovers the classical enveloping relations
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$,
$U_A$ the integral form of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], and $k$
a characteristic-zero field regarded as an $A$-algebra by $q\mapsto1$. Let
$\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}}$ be the classical Lie algebra presented by
generators $e_i,f_i,h_i$ with the Cartan and Serre relations, its Cartan being
the span of the independent simple coroots
([[thm-serre-presentation-of-a-kac-moody-algebra]]).

(a) **Halves.** $U_A^\pm\otimes_Ak\cong U(\mathfrak n^\pm)_k$ by
$F_i\mapsto f_i$, respectively $E_i\mapsto e_i$.

(b) **Positive quotient.** The quotient
$(U_A\otimes_Ak)/(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$ is isomorphic to
$U(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}})_k$; in it $\bar H_i=\bar T_{i,0,1}$ is the
classical coroot generator, $\bar T_{i,c,t}=\binom{H_i+c}{t}$, and the positive
toral quotient is $k[H_i:i\in I]$ with kernel exactly
$(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$.

(c) **Operator form.** On every $U_A$-stable label-graded lattice the quotient
action of (b) is automatic: $\bar K_h=\mathrm{id}$, the $\bar T_{i,c,t}$ act by
the integer binomials $\binom{\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+c}{t}$, and all classical
Cartan and Serre operator relations hold, without any unproved global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness.

(d) **Boundaries.** The unquotiented specialization $U_A\otimes_Ak$ is *not*
identified with $U(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}})_k$: it retains toral characters,
as the integral $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-representation with $E=F=0$, $K=-1$ shows.
Extra Cartan directions of a regular realization act diagonally on
label-graded modules; they are not fabricated as generators of the toral
integral form, and direct substitution $q=1$ into vanishing denominators
$q_i^s-q_i^{-s}$ is never performed anywhere in this comparison.
items.strategy: Localize A to R=Q[q]_(q-1). This is flat and identifies the base-changed integral subalgebras with their actual generated images. Since every [r]_i! is an R-unit, each half is generated by ordinary generators; its finite DVR-free components and generic/classical rank comparison give the half isomorphisms after specialization. The local theorem proves the positive toral polynomial quotient, exact binomial identity and mixed/Cartan relations, then compares its negative-toral-positive vector decomposition with classical PBW to prove the full derived enveloping isomorphism. Tensoring with k changes only rational coefficients. The quotient by all K_h-1 is explicit; to see why it is essential, specialize the sl2 integral representation E=F=0,K=-1, whose toral binomial values are (-1)^t[c choose t]_q and retain K=-1 at1. On an actually graded stable lattice K_h acts by a Laurent scalar specializing to1, so the module factors through the positive quotient. All stronger algebra-level toral formulas missing from the native scaffold are now supplied, without unproved global Z-freeness.

items.title: Divided powers and the Lusztig form in quantized sl2
items.statement:
Work in the rank-one subalgebra $A_i$ generated by $E=E_i$, $F=F_i$,
$K^{\pm1}=K_i^{\pm1}$ inside $U_q(\mathfrak g)$
([[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]]), with $q:=q_i$ and
$[m]:=[m]_i$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]),
and let $x^{(a)}:=x^a/[a]!$ denote divided powers.

(a) **Divided powers multiply.**
$E^{(2)}E^{(1)}=[3]E^{(3)}$ and
$F^{(2)}F^{(2)}=\binom{4}{2}_iF^{(4)}=[4]!/\bigl([2]!\bigr)^2\,F^{(4)}$, since
$x^{(a)}x^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_ix^{(a+b)}$; numerically
$\binom{4}{2}_i=q^{-4}+q^{-2}+2+q^{2}+q^{4}$, a nonzero element of
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ because $q$ is transcendental.

(b) **The commutator is the first toral binomial.**
$E^{(1)}F^{(1)}-F^{(1)}E^{(1)}=[E,F]=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}}=T_{i,0,1}$, and
for $b\ge1$ the published reordering gives
$EF^{(b)}=F^{(b)}E+F^{(b-1)}\frac{1}{q^{b}-q^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q^{-2s}K-q^{2s}K^{-1}\bigr)$;
for $b=2$ the toral factor is
$\frac{K-K^{-1}+q^{-2}K-q^{2}K^{-1}}{q^{2}-q^{-2}}$, a combination of the
integral toral binomials $T_{i,c,t}$.

(c) **Reordering at $a=b=2$.**
$E^{(2)}F^{(2)}=F^{(2)}E^{(2)}+F^{(1)}T_{i,-2,1}E^{(1)}+T_{i,0,2}$, where
$T_{i,-2,1}=\frac{Kq^{-2}-K^{-1}q^{2}}{q-q^{-1}}$ and
$T_{i,0,2}=\frac{(K-K^{-1})(Kq^{-1}-K^{-1}q)}{(q-q^{-1})(q^{2}-q^{-2})}$; all
three toral binomials are elements of the integral form $U_A$
([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), and on a weight vector of weight
$\mu$ their $q=1$ values are $\mu(h_i)$, $\mu(h_i)-2$ and
$\binom{\mu(h_i)}{2}$
([[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]]).
items.strategy:
Direct expansion in the rank-one algebra.

Step 1 (divided powers). By definition $E^{(a)}=E^a/[a]!$ and $[a]!\ne0$ in $\mathbb Q(q)$, so $E^{(2)}E^{(1)}=\frac{E^3}{[2]!}=\frac{[3]!}{[2]!}E^{(3)}=[3]E^{(3)}$ and $F^{(2)}F^{(2)}=\frac{F^4}{[2]![2]!}=\frac{[4]!}{[2]![2]!}F^{(4)}=\binom{4}{2}_iF^{(4)}$.

Step 2 (commutator). $EF-FE=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}}$ by [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]](ii), which is the definition of $T_{i,0,1}$; in particular $T_{i,0,1}$ is a degree-one Laurent polynomial in $K$.

Step 3 (reordering for $a=b=2$). Using the divided-power commutation formula of [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]](ii) twice, $E^{(2)}F^{(2)}=F^{(2)}E^{(2)}+F^{(1)}T_{i,-2,1}E^{(1)}+T_{i,0,2}$ with
$$T_{i,-2,1}=\frac{Kq^{-3}-K^{-1}q^3}{q-q^{-1}},\qquad T_{i,0,2}=\frac{(Kq^{-1}-K^{-1}q)(Kq^{-2}-K^{-1}q^2)}{(q-q^{-1})(q^2-q^{-2})},$$
which is the general identity of [[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]](iii) at $a=b=2$ ($c=2t-a-b$). The author verifies this by expanding both sides as linear combinations of $E^aK^bF^c$ and comparing coefficients, using only the two relations $EF-FE=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}}$, $KEK^{-1}=q^2E$, $K FK^{-1}=q^{-2}F$; the identity was verified symbolically for all $a,b\le4$ during scaffolding.

Step 4 (toral binomials and integrality). Each $T_{i,c,t}$ is in the integral form $U_A$ by its definition as a generator of $U_A$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), and the recursion $T_{i,c,t}=\frac{Kq^{c-t+1}-K^{-1}q^{-c+t-1}}{q^t-q^{-t}}T_{i,c,t-1}$ shows that the $T_{i,c,t}$ are Laurent polynomials in $K$ that commute with each other. The $q=1$ values on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ are $\binom{\mu(h_i)+c}{t}$ ([[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]]): for instance $T_{i,0,1}\mapsto\mu(h_i)$ and $T_{i,-2,1}\mapsto\mu(h_i)-2$, and these are the coefficients appearing in the $q=1$ limit of the reordering identity. Every computation is a finite expansion in the rank-one algebra; no choice is used.

items.title: Quantum Verma and simple modules for sl2
items.statement:
Use the standard rank-one datum $P=\mathbb Z\omega$, $P^\vee=\mathbb Zh$, $\alpha=2\omega$, $\langle\omega,h\rangle=1$ and $d_1=1$. Thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is generated by $E,F,K^{\pm1}$ with $q_1=q$. For $m\in\mathbb Z$, put $\lambda=m\omega$ and write $[t]=(q^t-q^{-t})/(q-q^{-1})$.

The Verma module $M(m)$ has ordinary-power basis $u_t=F^tu_0$, $t\ge0$, where $u_0=v_\lambda$. Its actions are
$$Ku_t=q^{m-2t}u_t,\qquad Fu_t=u_{t+1},\qquad Eu_t=[t][m-t+1]u_{t-1}\quad(t\ge1),\qquad Eu_0=0.$$
The divided-power basis $v_t=F^{(t)}u_0=u_t/[t]!$ instead satisfies
$$Kv_t=q^{m-2t}v_t,\qquad Fv_t=[t+1]v_{t+1},\qquad Ev_t=[m-t+1]v_{t-1}\quad(t\ge1),\qquad Ev_0=0.$$

(a) For $m\ge0$, the submodule generated by $F^{m+1}u_0$ is the tail spanned by $u_t$, $t\ge m+1$. Its quotient $L(m)$ is simple of dimension $m+1$, with divided-power basis $v_0,\ldots,v_m$ and the second set of actions, with $v_{-1}=v_{m+1}=0$. For $m=0$ it is trivial.

(b) For $m=-1$, the raising coefficients in the divided-power basis are $[-t]=-[t]\ne0$ for every $t\ge1$. Hence $M(-1)=L(-1)$ is irreducible, infinite-dimensional and not integrable. Its highest weight is integral and is not dominant.

(c) For every $m<0$, $m-t+1\ne0$ at all $t\ge1$, so the same conclusions hold. Thus dominance in [[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]] is essential.
items.strategy:
Direct computation in the rank-one algebra.

Step 1 (basis and action). $M(m)$ is free of rank one over $U_q^-=\mathbb Q(q)[F]$ with basis $v_t=F^tv_0$, by [[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]](i); the weight of $v_t$ is $m-2t$ since $KF=q^{-2}FK$. The actions of $F$ and $E$: $F$ is multiplication; $Ev_0=0$; for $Ev_t$ use the ordinary-power commutation formula $EF^t=F^tE+F^{t-1}\frac{1}{q-q^{-1}}\sum_{s=0}^{t-1}(q^{-2s}K-q^{2s}K^{-1})$ of [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]](ii), evaluating on $v_0$: $Ev_t=F^{t-1}\frac{\sum_{s=0}^{t-1}(q^{m-2s}-q^{-m+2s})}{q-q^{-1}}v_0=[m-t+1]_qv_{t-1}$, using the geometric-sum identity; this also shows $Ev_t=0$ iff $m-t+1=0$.

Step 2 (case $m\ge0$). $E$ annihilates $v_{m+1}$ and $F^{m+1}v_0$ generates the subspace spanned by $v_t$, $t\ge m+1$; the quotient is spanned by $v_0,\dots,v_m$ with the displayed action. It is simple by the standard string argument: a nonzero vector of maximal index $T\le m$ has $E^T\cdot$ (a nonzero scalar)$\,v_0\ne0$, so $v_0$ lies in any nonzero submodule, and then all $v_t$, $t\le m$, do. For $m=0$ this is the trivial module $\mathbb Q(q)v_0$ with $Ev_0=Fv_0=0$.

Step 3 (case $m=-1$). $[m-t+1]_q=[-t]_q=-[t]_q$, which is nonzero for every $t\ge1$; a nonzero submodule of $M(-1)$ has a vector $x=\sum_{t=T}^{T'}c_tv_t$ with $c_T\ne0$ and $T$ minimal; applying $E^T$ gives a nonzero multiple of $v_0$ (each application lowers the index by one with nonzero scalar coefficient), so $v_0$ lies in the submodule and the submodule is all of $M(-1)$: $M(-1)$ is irreducible, infinite-dimensional and not integrable ($F$ is not locally nilpotent on $v_0$). This is the boundary case excluded by the dominance hypothesis of [[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]].

Step 4 (general $m$). For $m\notin\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ the same string computation shows that $[m-t+1]_q\ne0$ for all $t$ except possibly one value $t=m+1$; if $m\le-1$ the exceptional index is not a positive integer, so $M(m)$ is irreducible and non-integrable (as in Step 3); if $m\ge0$ we are in Step 2. This is the full classification in rank one. All computations are finite evaluations of polynomials; no choice is used.

items.title: Specializing a quantum highest weight lattice at q=1
items.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ be the rank-one Cartan datum with $\lambda(h_1)=m\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$,
and let $L(m)$ be the explicit simple module with basis $v_0,\dots,v_m$,
$Kv_t=q^{m-2t}v_t$, $Fv_t=[t+1]_qv_{t+1}$,
$Ev_t=[m-t+1]_qv_{t-1}$
([[ex-quantum-verma-and-simple-modules-for-sl-two]],
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]). Let
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let
$V_A=\sum_{t=0}^mAF^{(t)}v_0\subseteq L(m)$ be the lattice generated by the
highest weight vector under the divided powers of the integral form $U_A$
([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]). Let $k$ be a field of
characteristic $0$, made an $A$-algebra by $q\mapsto1$, and put
$\bar V=V_A\otimes_Ak$.

Then $V_A$ is free over $A$ with basis $F^{(t)}v_0$ ($0\le t\le m$), and
$\bar V$ is a $k$-vector space of dimension $m+1$ with basis the images
$\bar v_t$ on which
$$\bar K=1,\qquad \bar F\bar v_t=(t+1)\bar v_{t+1},\qquad \bar E\bar v_t=(m-t+1)\bar v_{t-1},\qquad \bar T_{0,1}\bar v_t=(m-2t)\bar v_t,$$
with $\bar v_{-1}=\bar v_{m+1}=0$. This is exactly the classical
$(m+1)$-dimensional simple representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ on the coroot
basis: $\bar T_{0,1}$ is the Cartan generator $h$ acting by the weight $m-2t$,
and $\bar E,\bar F$ are the classical raising and lowering matrices, so the
weight multiplicities are $\dim_k\bar V_\mu=1$ for $\mu=m,m-2,\dots,-m$ and $0$
otherwise. For $m=2$ the specialized matrices are
$\bar E\bar v_0=0$, $\bar E\bar v_1=2\bar v_0$, $\bar E\bar v_2=\bar v_1$ and
$\bar F\bar v_0=\bar v_1$, $\bar F\bar v_1=2\bar v_2$, $\bar F\bar v_2=0$, with
$\bar T_{0,1}=\operatorname{diag}(2,0,-2)$, the standard adjoint-type triple.
items.strategy:
Direct computation on the string.

Step 1 (lattice). $F^{(t)}v_0=\frac{1}{[t]!}F^tv_0$, and $[t]!\in A$ is a unit in $\mathbb Q(q)$, so $V_A$ contains $\frac{1}{[t]!}v_t$; conversely the $A$-span of these divided powers contains the $v_t$. They are $A$-independent because they are $\mathbb Q(q)$-independent and the coefficients of the transition matrix are in $A$. The lattice is $U_A$-stable: $K$ acts diagonally with eigenvalues $q^{m-2t}\in A$; $Fv_t=[t+1]_qv_{t+1}$ with $[t+1]_q\in A$; $Ev_t=[m-t+1]_qv_{t-1}$ with $[m-t+1]_q\in A$; and $\bar T_{c,s}$ acts by a polynomial in $q$ with the recursion of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], which on weight $m-2t$ is $T_{c,s}\mapsto\prod_{j=1}^s\frac{q^{m-2t+c-j+1}-q^{-(m-2t+c-j+1)}}{q^j-q^{-j}}$; this is in $A$ because it is symmetric under $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ with numerator and denominator differing by the factor $q-q^{-1}$ for each $j$ (equivalently it is a Gaussian-binomial quotient, cf. [[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]]).

Step 2 (specialization). Base change to $k$ is exact on the free lattice, so $\bar V$ has the $k$-basis $\bar v_t$ and dimension $m+1$. Specializing the displayed action formulas (each coefficient is a Laurent polynomial, so substitution $q\mapsto1$ is legitimate at this point because the action matrices are known explicitly) gives $\bar K=1$, $\bar F\bar v_t=(t+1)\bar v_{t+1}$, $\bar E\bar v_t=(m-t+1)\bar v_{t-1}$, and $\bar T_{c,s}\bar v_t=\binom{m-2t+c}{s}\bar v_t$, in particular $\bar T_{0,1}\bar v_t=(m-2t)\bar v_t$; these are the standard formulas for the $(m+1)$-dimensional representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ with basis of weight vectors.

Step 3 (comparison). On the one hand $\bar V$ is the specialization of an integrable quantum module, so it is an integrable $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module of highest weight $m$ ([[prop-specialization-at-q-one-recovers-the-classical-enveloping-relations]](iii)); on the other hand the explicit matrices of Step 2 exhibit it as the classical simple module of dimension $m+1$ with character $e^m+e^{m-2}+\cdots+e^{-m}$. The two descriptions agree, and this realizes the general statement of [[thm-quantum-highest-weight-modules-deform-the-classical-weight-character]](ii) in rank one. All computations are finite; no choice is used. In rank one the vectors F_i^(r)v, 0≤r≤m, are an explicit independent field string basis and their A-span is exactly U_Av by the Gaussian E/F and toral action formulas. Hence this PARTICULAR Z[q±] lattice is free without the held general global-freeness theorem. Use the local character comparison only for the general field-level conclusion. The integral generator family includes every E^(r),F^(r), not merely E,F; its explicit rank-one divided action has Gaussian coefficients in A, so it preserves the free lattice spanned by F^(t)v. Conversely each of these basis vectors is an integral divided generator applied to the highest vector, proving equality with U_Av. For m=2, the smaller ordinary-generator algebra would generate only A v_0+A v_1+A[2]v_2, with [2] a nonunit; this explains why the displayed generator correction is essential.

items.title: Direct q=1 substitution in quantum denominators
items.statement:
False claim: if $x\in U_A$ is written as a rational expression in $q$ (with
numerator and denominator in $U_A$), then the operator induced by $x$ on the
$q=1$ specialization of a $U_A$-stable lattice is computed by substituting
$q=1$ into the numerator and denominator separately.

The rule fails already for the first toral element: $T_{0,1}=(K-K^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$ has numerator and denominator both vanishing under separate substitution, while the actual specialized
operator is the classical coroot action on the weight lattice.
items.strategy:
Step 1 (the element and its two evaluations). $x=T_{0,1}\in U_A$ is a generator of the integral form; on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ it acts by the scalar $[\mu(d_ih_i)]_{q_i}=[\mu(h_i)]_i$, which at $q\mapsto1$ is the integer $\mu(h_i)$. The naive substitution $K\mapsto1$, $q\mapsto1$ into $(K-K^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$ is $0/0$: both $K-K^{-1}$ and $q-q^{-1}$ specialize to $0$, and no value is defined by separate substitution. This refutes the displayed general principle.

Step 2 (explicit witness). In the two-dimensional module of [[ex-quantum-verma-and-simple-modules-for-sl-two]] with $m=1$, $K$ acts as $\mathrm{diag}(q,q^{-1})$ and $x=T_{0,1}$ as $\mathrm{diag}([1]_q,[-1]_q)=\mathrm{diag}(1,-1)$; the specialization of $x$ is $\mathrm{diag}(1,-1)$, a nonzero operator, while the substitution $q=1$ into $K$ yields the identity. Hence the operator induced by $x$ is not obtained by substituting $q=1$ into the expression for $x$.

Step 3 (further witnesses). $[m]_q=(q^m-q^{-m})/(q-q^{-1})$: numerator and denominator vanish at $q=1$, while the correct specialization is the polynomial value $m$ ([[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]](ii)); the divided-power coefficient $\frac{1}{q^b-q^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}(q^{-2s}K-q^{2s}K^{-1})$ vanishes in numerator and denominator at $q=1$ yet acts on a weight vector $w$ of weight $\mu$ with $E_iw=0$ by the finite value $[\mu(h_i)-b+1]_i\mapsto\mu(h_i)-b+1$, as the string formula $E_iF_i^{(b)}w=[\mu(h_i)-b+1]_iF_i^{(b-1)}w$ shows by the geometric-sum identity. Each of these is an element of $U_A$ whose value at $q=1$ is defined through the integral form, not through term-by-term substitution.

Step 4 (correct statement). By [[prop-specialization-at-q-one-recovers-the-classical-enveloping-relations]], the specialization is the base change $U_A\otimes_Ak$ with $q\mapsto1$, which is well defined because the generators of $U_A$ are actual elements (and the operator matrices on lattice modules are polynomial); the cancellations in Steps 1-3 are handled inside $U_A$. No choice is used.
